# External hooks

<!-- Generated by `go run docs/roadmap/gen.go docs` from tickets.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

**Phase:** [P4 · Agents everywhere](../README.md#phase-4--agents-everywhere) · **Lane:** Worker · **Label:** `feature:policy-hooks` · **Epic:** [#207](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/207) · **Tickets:** 11 (3S 8M)

Operators can attach external checks at connect time, before a request is forwarded, and after a response returns: CEL expressions, OPA (REST or embedded) and signed webhooks. Hooks can only add denies, never allow something policy, identity, judge, MCP or DLP denied. Each hook has a timeout and a fail mode that defaults to closed, and a destination a matching hook cannot inspect is denied rather than passed.

## How we build it

- Scope and gate: new package internal/hooks. Default off: with no `settings.hooks` and no local `hooks:` YAML block, GET /policy, its ETag and the request path are byte-identical (golden test) and the no-hook path adds one atomic load and zero allocations (benchmark). Hooks run only after the existing policy, identity, block-list, scoped-policy, user-limit, judge, MCP and DLP verdicts allow, so a hook can never turn Deny, NoMatch or Conditional into Allow. Pre hooks run before swapSecrets, so no hook ever sees a real secret value.
- Types: `Hook` interface `Name() string` and `Evaluate(ctx, Input) (Result, error)`; `Result{Deny bool, Reason string}` with the reason stripped of control characters and capped at 256 bytes. An immutable `Chain` per settings apply, held on Proxy in a new atomic holder `hooksP` (same pattern as judgeP and secretsP) and snapshotted once per request. Closed `Input` struct, schema `warden.hook.v1`: request_id, stage, agent_id, identity {status, sub, email (only with includeEmail and a verified token), groups (cap 64), act} from the P1 identity.Subject; grant_id from identity.Subject.GrantID (set by W-P4-DGR-05 on grant tokens; empty otherwise); protocol, domain, port, method, path (from the pre-swap auditURL of W-P1-JAUD-05, no query or userinfo, max 2 KiB), mcp {method, tools[]}, dlp_classes, finding_kinds; the post stage adds response {status, content_type, scanned, dlp_classes, finding_kinds}. Headers, query values, bodies and identity tokens are never in Input.
- Stages and coverage: `connect` runs in handleConn after the block-list, identity and policy checks and before any dial, using domain, port and identity only, so it covers every protocol including raw tunnels. `pre` runs per HTTP/1.1 request in a new `hookGate` stage after dlpScan and before swapSecrets, and per h2 stream at the top of serveGRPCStream before the header swap. Tool-matching pre hooks also run for MCP over WebSocket and the local stdio wrapper through a decorator around the MCP gateway verdict, and in the MCP hub before tools/call is routed. When a pre hook matches a destination whose connection cannot be inspected (no CA, non-TLS, unknown protocol inside TLS, or an h2/WebSocket path not yet wired), the connection is denied with `hook_uninspectable`; the `deferred` enum from W-P1-GPOL-03 gains the value `hooks`.
- Post stage: `post` hooks run in relayResponse after response headers are read and after any buffered MCP or HTTP response scan, before the first byte reaches the agent, for every response except a 101 handoff. They can deny buffered and streamed responses; body-derived fields are filled only when the body was buffered and `response.scanned` says which. A deny returns 502 JSON (or a JSON-RPC error for MCP) to match the existing response denies, and the upstream connection is closed. Findings that appear later inside an SSE stream are not re-evaluated. Post hooks protect the agent from responses; they cannot undo upstream side effects.
- Config: `hooks: [{name, stage: connect|pre|post, type: cel|opa|webhook, match: {agents, domains (policy.MatchDomain dialect), tools, groups}, timeout (default 200ms, max 2s), failMode: open|closed (default closed), includeArgs (default false), includeEmail (default false), exposeReason (default false), ...type fields}]` and `hooksBudget: {connect: 300ms, pre: 500ms, post: 300ms}` (each max 2s), in strict local YAML and in SettingsWire (json omitempty, carried by SettingsWireFromPolicy and DeepCopy). One validator in internal/config runs on CP save and on worker apply: names match `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}$` and are unique, at most 16 hooks, CEL and rego compile, includeArgs only for in-process types, https URLs unless the host is loopback. Editing `hooks` is admin-only (W-P1-SSO-05) and audited (p1-admin-audit) with URL hosts only.
- Execution: in-process hooks (CEL, embedded OPA) run first in config order and stop at the first deny. Remote hooks (webhook, OPA REST) then run in parallel with golang.org/x/sync/errgroup under min(per-hook timeout, remaining stage budget); the reported deny is the first by config order. Each remote hook has one keep-alive client with an in-flight cap (default 64, overflow is error kind `overload`) and a circuit breaker (5 consecutive errors open it for 30s, during which failMode applies without a call). Every error, timeout, overload, open circuit or budget exhaustion goes to failMode: closed denies with `hook_unavailable`; open passes, records the hook in Event.HookFailOpen and counts it. Total stage time goes to warden.request.added_latency{stage=hooks_connect|hooks_pre|hooks_post}.
- CEL (`type: cel`): github.com/google/cel-go with declared variables `request`, `identity`, `mcp` (with `mcp.args` only when includeArgs is set) and `response` (post only). `denyIf` (max 4 KiB) is compiled once per apply and must type-check to bool; optional static `reason`. Programs use cel.CostLimit (default 10000, max 1e6) and cel.InterruptCheckFrequency and are evaluated with ContextEval under the hook deadline. Tool args for includeArgs come from the pre-swap, post-redaction request body, capped at 64 KiB.
- OPA (`type: opa`): `mode: rest` POSTs `{"input": Input}` to `{url}/v1/data/{path}` with an optional bearer token from `tokenEnv`. `mode: embedded` uses github.com/open-policy-agent/opa/v1/rego with modules inline in settings (cap 256 KiB total, so they ride the signed bundle and approvals); `bundlePath` (max 8 MiB) is allowed only in standalone local YAML. Embedded queries are prepared once per apply with restricted capabilities that remove opa.runtime, http.send, net.*, print and trace, plus StrictBuiltinErrors, so rego can never read the worker environment or send data out. A result is a bool or an object {deny, reason}; an undefined result or any other shape is error kind `malformed`, never an allow.
- Webhook (`type: webhook`): a new leaf package internal/webhooksig provides `Sign` and `Verify` for the existing v1 scheme (X-Warden-Timestamp, X-Warden-Signature = v1=hex(hmac-sha256(secret, ts + "." + body))); internal/integration/webhook moves to it with byte-identical output. Hook webhooks must be signed: `secretEnv` names an env var resolved on the worker (like llmProviders apiKeyEnv), the value never travels on the wire, and a missing value is a build error. Requests carry the Input JSON plus X-Warden-Hook (name) and X-Warden-Hook-Id (request id for replay dedupe); the response is `{decision: allow|deny, reason}`. Remote hook clients dial through a SafeDialer injected from internal/worker (proxy.NewSafeDialer with private CIDRs listed only in local worker YAML `hooksAllowPrivate`), set Proxy=nil, follow no redirects and cap responses at 64 KiB. Logs show the URL host only.
- Hot reload and degraded modes: SettingsApplier rebuilds the chain only when the canonical hash of the hooks block changes, so breakers survive unrelated applies. If a hook fails to build on a worker, the previous compiled hook is kept with one WARN; if there is none (first apply or restart), an always-error placeholder is installed so failMode decides and the hook is never dropped silently. CP down: hooks run from last-known-good settings or the signed bundle (p2-signed-bundles). IdP down: Input carries identity.status and hooks may deny anonymous traffic.
- Rollout and back-compat: workers add heartbeat cap `hooks/v1` (caps list from W-P1-BLOCK-02). The CP refuses a save that adds or changes hooks while a connected worker lacks the cap (409 workers_lack_capability, admin-only audited force, the W-P2-WBND-07 pattern), and the fleet view flags such workers. Old binaries fail at startup on a local `hooks:` block (KnownFields). Hooks ride policy-as-code and canary rollouts (p4-gitops) unchanged; policyeval replay reports that hooks were not replayed and counts recorded hook denies as deny.
- Recording and observability: bounded reasons `hook_denied`, `hook_unavailable` and `hook_uninspectable` join internal/proxy/reasons.go (W-P1-JAUD-06) and the decision.v1 reason enum. New fields Event.Hook, Event.HookReason (sanitized, kept apart from JudgeReason) and Event.HookFailOpen (json omitempty), mapped into auditlog.Record and docs/schemas/warden.decision.v1.json with a schema_rev bump. The agent sees `{"error":"hook_denied","hook":"<name>"}`, with the reason only when exposeReason is set. OTel instruments (exported as warden_hook_*): warden.hook.duration{hook,stage}, warden.hook.decisions.total{hook,stage,decision}, warden.hook.errors.total{hook,kind=timeout|budget|transport|status|malformed|cost|overload|circuit_open|build}, warden.hook.fail_open.total{hook}, gauge warden.hook.circuit_open{hook}. Labels use configured names only, never sub, email or groups; Input is never logged above debug.

## Done when

On a managed deployment where every worker reports `hooks/v1`: a CEL, an embedded OPA, a REST OPA and a signed webhook hook can each deny a request the policy allowed over HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2/gRPC and MCP over HTTP and WebSocket, recorded with Reason hook_denied and the hook name; destinations a matching hook cannot inspect are denied with hook_uninspectable; no hook can make a policy-denied, NoMatch or Conditional request succeed; a timed-out, erroring or circuit-open hook follows its failMode (closed denies with hook_unavailable, open passes and records hook_fail_open on the event and in metrics); a post hook can block a response before any byte reaches the agent; remote hooks never receive bodies, args or real secrets and embedded rego cannot read the worker environment or make network calls; a broken hook config never silently removes a hook; and with no hooks configured the policy ETag and request path are byte-identical.

### 1/11 · W-P4-HOOK-01

**Add hook framework, config and metrics**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#208](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/208)

Create internal/hooks with the Hook interface, the closed Input struct, Result and a Chain that applies per-hook timeouts, per-stage budgets and failMode, and can only return deny or pass. Add the `hooks` and `hooksBudget` config blocks to strict YAML and SettingsWire with one shared validator, and register the hook metrics. The type registry is empty in this ticket, so any configured hook fails validation and the ticket ships inert.

**Requirements**

- New internal/hooks/hooks.go: `Hook` interface `Name() string`, `InProcess() bool`, `Evaluate(ctx context.Context, in Input) (Result, error)`; `Result{Deny bool, Reason string}`; a `Sanitize` helper strips control characters and caps reasons at 256 bytes.
- Closed `Input` struct (schema `warden.hook.v1`) with request_id, stage, agent_id, identity {status, sub, email, groups (cap 64), act}, grant_id, protocol, domain, port, method, path (max 2 KiB), mcp {method, tools[], args (json.RawMessage, in-process only)}, dlp_classes, finding_kinds and response {status, content_type, scanned, dlp_classes, finding_kinds}. No header, query, body or token field exists.
- New internal/hooks/chain.go: `Chain.Run(ctx, stage, Input) Decision{Deny, Hook, Kind, Reason, FailOpen []string}`. In-process hooks run first in config order and stop at the first deny; remote hooks run in parallel with errgroup and the first deny by config order wins. Each hook gets min(timeout, remaining stage budget); a hook not started because the budget is spent is kind `budget` under its own failMode. A panicking hook is an error. No code path turns a deny into an allow.
- Config in new internal/config/hooks.go: `HookConfig{Name, Stage, Type, Match{Agents, Domains, Tools, Groups}, Timeout, FailMode, IncludeArgs, IncludeEmail, ExposeReason}` and `HooksBudget{Connect, Pre, Post}` with defaults 200ms timeout, failMode closed, budgets 300/500/300ms, all max 2s. Strict YAML through the existing KnownFields decoder; `SettingsWire.Hooks` and `SettingsWire.HooksBudget` (json omitempty) are carried by SettingsWireFromPolicy and copied by DeepCopy.
- One exported validator `config.ValidateHooks` used by worker apply now and by the CP save in W-P4-HOOK-10: name regex `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}$`, unique names, at most 16 hooks, stage connect|pre|post, connect hooks may match only agents, domains and groups, includeArgs only for in-process types, and `type` checked against a registry that types add themselves to.
- Nil-safe metrics in internal/observability/observability.go: `RecordHookDecision(hook, stage, decision)`, `RecordHookError(hook, kind)`, `RecordHookFailOpen(hook)`, `ObserveHookDuration(hook, stage, d)` and `SetHookCircuitOpen(hook, open)`, as OTel instruments warden.hook.duration, warden.hook.decisions.total, warden.hook.errors.total, warden.hook.fail_open.total and warden.hook.circuit_open. Chain records them; logs carry hook name, kind and duration only.
- Performance: Chain overhead excluding the hooks' own work is p99 under 20µs for 4 in-process fake hooks; a Chain with no hook matching the Input allocates nothing (benchmark).

**Implementation plan**

1. Add new internal/hooks/hooks.go with Hook, Input, Result, Decision, Sanitize and a type registry `Register(typ string, build BuildFunc)` used by later tickets.
2. Add new internal/hooks/match.go: match on agents, groups, tools and domains using policy.MatchDomain; precompute per-stage hook slices at build time so a non-matching Input costs no allocation.
3. Add new internal/hooks/chain.go with `Build(cfg []config.HookConfig, budget config.HooksBudget, deps Deps) (*Chain, []error)` and `Run`, using context.WithTimeout per hook and errgroup for remote hooks.
4. Add new internal/config/hooks.go with HookConfig, HooksBudget, defaults and ValidateHooks; add the `hooks`/`hooksBudget` keys to the YAML root in internal/config/config.go and to SettingsWire, SettingsWireFromPolicy and DeepCopy in internal/config/settings.go.
5. Add the hook instruments and Record/Observe methods to internal/observability/observability.go next to RecordBlocked and ObserveAddedLatency.
6. Write internal/hooks/chain_test.go with fake in-process and remote hooks, internal/config/hooks_test.go for validation and the wire round trip, and BenchmarkChainNoMatch.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given fake hooks, a deny short-circuits the remaining in-process hooks, and with two remote denies the first by config order is reported: `go test ./internal/hooks -run TestChain_DenyOrder`.
- [ ] A hook that sleeps past its 200ms timeout denies with Kind timeout under failMode closed and passes with FailOpen set under failMode open, and warden.hook.errors.total{kind=timeout} increments in both cases: `go test ./internal/hooks -run TestChain_TimeoutFailMode`.
- [ ] With three sequential 300ms in-process hooks and a 500ms pre budget, the third hook is never invoked and is recorded as kind budget under its own failMode: `go test ./internal/hooks -run TestChain_Budget`.
- [ ] Validation rejects an unknown key, a duplicate name, a bad name, more than 16 hooks, a timeout above 2s and any `type` while the registry is empty; a settings value without hooks round-trips byte-identical through SettingsWireFromPolicy and DeepCopy: `go test ./internal/config -run TestHooksConfig`.
- [ ] `go test ./internal/hooks -run '^$' -bench BenchmarkChainNoMatch -benchmem` reports 0 allocs/op.

**Unblocks:** [`W-P4-HOOK-07`](policy-hooks.md#711--w-p4-hook-07) Wire the pre-request hook stage into the HTTP/1.1 proxy path

### 2/11 · W-P4-HOOK-02

**Add CEL hook type**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#209](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/209)

Register `type: cel` so operators can write in-process deny rules such as group or tool checks without running a service. Expressions are compiled and type-checked once per apply, bounded by a cost limit and the hook deadline. This ticket also adds tool-argument extraction for `includeArgs`, which in-process hooks share.

**Requirements**

- Config fields `denyIf` (CEL source, max 4 KiB), optional static `reason` (max 256 bytes) and `costLimit` (default 10000, max 1e6). Uses github.com/google/cel-go/cel pinned to a release at least two weeks old.
- Declared variables `request`, `identity`, `mcp` (with `mcp.args` only when includeArgs is true) and `response` (only for stage post). An expression whose output type is not bool, or that references an undeclared variable, fails ValidateHooks with the hook name and the CEL error position.
- Programs are built once per settings apply with cel.CostLimit and cel.InterruptCheckFrequency and shared across requests; evaluation uses ContextEval under the hook deadline. Exceeding the cost limit is error kind `cost`, any other runtime error kind `eval`, both under failMode.
- includeArgs: a new bounded helper in internal/mcp returns the raw tools/call `arguments` from the pre-swap, post-redaction request body (s.reqBody), capped at 64 KiB; larger args are absent and recorded as kind `malformed`. Args carry only placeholder names, never real secrets.
- The hook also derives the tool name with protocol.IsMCP when the MCP gateway is off (s.gw == nil), so match.tools still works; validation warns once when a hook uses match.tools and MCP is disabled.
- The expression source is never logged at INFO or above. Performance: a groups-membership expression evaluates with p99 under 50µs.

**Implementation plan**

1. Add github.com/google/cel-go to go.mod.
2. Add new internal/hooks/cel.go: build cel.NewEnv with the declared variables, compile denyIf, reject when the output type is not cel.BoolType, and Register("cel", ...).
3. Create the program with env.Program(ast, cel.CostLimit(n), cel.InterruptCheckFrequency(100)) and evaluate with prg.ContextEval(ctx, vars) built from Input.
4. Add new `ToolCallArgs(body []byte, max int) (json.RawMessage, bool)` in internal/mcp next to the existing ToolCall parsing, and fill Input.MCP.Args only for in-process hooks with includeArgs.
5. Wire the CEL check into config.ValidateHooks so the CP save path (W-P4-HOOK-10) compiles expressions too.
6. Write internal/hooks/cel_test.go and BenchmarkCELHook; add example configs under new internal/hooks/testdata/examples for the docs ticket.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] A syntax error, an unknown variable or a non-bool expression fails validation with an error naming the hook: `go test ./internal/config -run TestHooksConfig_CEL`.
- [ ] With `denyIf: "'contractors' in identity.groups"`, a member of contractors is denied with Reason hook_denied and a non-member is allowed: `go test ./internal/hooks -run TestCEL_GroupsDeny`.
- [ ] A nested comprehension over a large list stops at the cost limit with kind cost, and failMode closed denies: `go test ./internal/hooks -run TestCEL_CostLimit`.
- [ ] With includeArgs false, an expression referencing `mcp.args` fails validation; with it true, args contain the placeholder name and not the secret value: `go test ./internal/hooks -run TestCEL_ArgsGated`.
- [ ] `go test ./internal/hooks -run '^$' -bench BenchmarkCELHook -benchmem` reports under 50µs/op.

**Depends on:** [`W-P4-HOOK-07`](policy-hooks.md#711--w-p4-hook-07) Wire the pre-request hook stage into the HTTP/1.1 proxy path

### 3/11 · W-P4-HOOK-03

**Add signed webhook hook type**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#210](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/210)

Register `type: webhook` so an external service can deny requests from the bounded Input. The existing v1 HMAC scheme moves to a new leaf package so both alerts and hooks use it, and hook calls are always signed with a secret resolved from the worker's own environment. The shared remote client built here (SSRF-safe dialer, no redirects, size cap, in-flight cap, circuit breaker) is reused by OPA REST.

**Requirements**

- New leaf package internal/webhooksig with `Sign(secret []byte, ts string, body []byte) string`, `Verify(secret []byte, ts, sig string, body []byte, now time.Time, tolerance time.Duration) error` and the X-Warden-Timestamp/X-Warden-Signature header constants. internal/integration/webhook switches to it and its signatures stay byte-identical.
- Config: `url` (https required; http only for a loopback host) and `secretEnv` (required env var name resolved on the worker; empty or unresolved is a build error, so the always-error placeholder applies). The secret value never appears on the wire, in logs or in errors. includeArgs is rejected.
- Request: POST of the JSON Input with Content-Type application/json and headers X-Warden-Timestamp, X-Warden-Signature, X-Warden-Hook (name) and X-Warden-Hook-Id (request id). Bodies, args, headers and tokens are never sent; email only with includeEmail.
- Response: 2xx JSON of at most 64 KiB shaped `{decision: allow|deny, reason?}`. Non-2xx, a redirect (never followed), bad JSON or an unknown decision is error kind status, malformed or transport under failMode. Reasons go through Sanitize.
- New internal/hooks/remote.go: one keep-alive http.Client per hook with Proxy=nil, a DialContext injected from internal/worker (proxy.NewSafeDialer with CIDRs from local-only worker YAML `hooksAllowPrivate`), CheckRedirect returning http.ErrUseLastResponse, an in-flight cap (default 64, overflow kind overload) and a circuit breaker (5 consecutive errors open it for 30s with one probe after; while open, kind circuit_open under failMode, gauge warden.hook.circuit_open set).
- Logs and errors contain the URL host only, never the full URL, payload or secret. Hook traffic never goes through the agent-facing proxy.

**Implementation plan**

1. Add new internal/webhooksig/webhooksig.go by moving `sign` and the header constants out of internal/integration/webhook/webhook.go; update that file to call webhooksig.Sign and add a golden test for unchanged output.
2. Add new internal/hooks/remote.go with the client, breaker and in-flight semaphore, taking the dialer through hooks.Deps.
3. Build the dialer in internal/worker wiring (proxy.NewSafeDialer(timeout, cfg.HooksAllowPrivate)) and pass it in Deps; add `hooksAllowPrivate` to the local worker YAML only, never to SettingsWire.
4. Add new internal/hooks/webhook.go: marshal Input with Args nil, sign the exact bytes, POST, parse the response, and Register("webhook", ...).
5. Extend config.ValidateHooks for url scheme, secretEnv presence and the includeArgs rejection.
6. Write internal/hooks/webhook_test.go with httptest.NewTLSServer receivers and internal/webhooksig/webhooksig_test.go.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] A receiver using webhooksig.Verify with a 300s tolerance accepts the request, and a tampered body or a timestamp older than 300s fails: `go test ./internal/hooks -run TestWebhook_SignatureVerifies`.
- [ ] The alert webhook signature for fixed inputs is unchanged: `go test ./internal/integration/webhook -run TestSign_Golden`.
- [ ] A receiver returning 500, a 302, invalid JSON or `{"decision":"maybe"}` triggers failMode and records the matching error kind: `go test ./internal/hooks -run TestWebhook_ErrorsFollowFailMode`.
- [ ] After 5 consecutive errors the next call is not sent, kind circuit_open is recorded and failMode applies: `go test ./internal/hooks -run TestRemote_CircuitBreaker`.
- [ ] For an MCP tools/call with arguments, the received body has the tool name but no args, request body, Authorization or query values: `go test ./internal/hooks -run TestWebhook_InputHasNoBodies`.
- [ ] A URL resolving to 169.254.169.254 or 10.0.0.0/8 without hooksAllowPrivate is refused at dial time, and a missing secretEnv value installs an always-error hook: `go test ./internal/hooks -run TestWebhook_SSRFAndSecret`.

**Depends on:** [`W-P4-HOOK-07`](policy-hooks.md#711--w-p4-hook-07) Wire the pre-request hook stage into the HTTP/1.1 proxy path

### 4/11 · W-P4-HOOK-04

**Add OPA REST hook type**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#211](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/211)

Register `type: opa` with `mode: rest` so operators can ask an existing OPA server for a deny decision. It reuses the remote client from the webhook ticket and shares one result parser with embedded mode (W-P4-HOOK-11). An undefined or malformed result is always an error under failMode, never an allow.

**Requirements**

- Config: `mode: rest`, `url` (same https/loopback rule as webhooks), `path` (validated dot or slash data path) and optional `tokenEnv` for a bearer token resolved on the worker.
- Request: `POST {url}/v1/data/{path}` with body `{"input": Input}`, through the shared remote client (injected SafeDialer, no redirects, 64 KiB response cap, in-flight cap, circuit breaker).
- New shared parser: `result` is a bool (deny = value) or an object `{deny bool, reason string}`. A missing `result` (undefined document) or any other shape is error kind malformed under failMode. Docs tell operators to define `default deny := false`.
- includeArgs and `modules`/`bundlePath` are rejected for mode rest.
- Logs show the URL host and data path only; the bearer token is never logged.

**Implementation plan**

1. Add new internal/hooks/opa_result.go with `parseOPAResult(raw json.RawMessage) (Result, error)`.
2. Add new internal/hooks/opa_rest.go using remote.go and Register("opa", ...) with a mode switch that rejects `embedded` until W-P4-HOOK-11 lands.
3. Extend config.ValidateHooks with OPA fields (mode, path, tokenEnv) and the includeArgs rejection for rest.
4. Write internal/hooks/opa_rest_test.go with an httptest server returning each result shape.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] An httptest /v1/data server returning `true`, `false` and `{deny:true, reason:"x"}` yields deny, pass and deny with reason x: `go test ./internal/hooks -run TestOPARest_ResultShapes`.
- [ ] An undefined result, a string or `{deny:"yes"}` returns kind malformed and failMode closed denies: `go test ./internal/hooks -run TestOPA_MalformedResult`.
- [ ] includeArgs with mode rest and `mode: embedded` (before W-P4-HOOK-11) fail validation: `go test ./internal/config -run TestHooksConfig_OPA`.
- [ ] The request carries Input without args and an Authorization header only when tokenEnv is set: `go test ./internal/hooks -run TestOPARest_Request`.

**Depends on:** [`W-P4-HOOK-03`](policy-hooks.md#311--w-p4-hook-03) Add signed webhook hook type

### 5/11 · W-P4-HOOK-05

**Add post-response hooks**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#212](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/212)

Run `stage: post` hooks in relayResponse after response headers and any buffered response scan, before the first byte reaches the agent, so they can block buffered and streamed responses alike. A deny returns 502 (or a JSON-RPC error for MCP) to match the existing response denies and closes the upstream. Post hooks protect the agent from responses; the upstream has already received the request, so they cannot undo side effects.

**Requirements**

- Post hooks run under hooksBudget.post (default 300ms) for every response except a 101 handoff, after mcpResponseScan/httpResponseScan buffering and before relayMCPSSE writes headers or finishResponse calls resp.Write.
- Input.response carries status, content_type, `scanned` (true only when the body was buffered) and, when scanned, the response DLP classes and MCP result finding kinds. No hook of any type receives the response body.
- Streamed or unbuffered responses (SSE, chunked, over the scan cap) are never buffered just to run hooks; post hooks evaluate once on status and content type and can deny then. Findings that appear later inside an SSE stream are not re-evaluated.
- Deny writes 502 JSON `{"error":"hook_denied","hook":"<name>"}` or a JSON-RPC error for MCP, sets closeAfter so the upstream conn is not reused, and stores one event with Reason hook_denied (or hook_unavailable), Event.Hook and ResponseStatus.
- A 101 WebSocket handoff skips post hooks and increments a new counter warden.hook.skipped.total{reason=websocket}.
- added_latency stage=hooks_post is recorded; with no post hooks configured the response path is unchanged with 0 extra allocations.

**Implementation plan**

1. Add new requestScope fields respDLPClasses and respFindingKinds in internal/proxy/http.go, filled where recordMCPFindings and recordResponseFindings run.
2. Add new `postHookGate(s *requestScope) (denied bool)` in new internal/proxy/hooks_post.go that builds the post Input and runs Chain.Run(stage post).
3. Call postHookGate in relayResponse after the buffering scans and before relayMCPSSE/finishResponse; skip on 101.
4. On deny reuse the existing response-deny branch shape from httpResponseScan (502, recordEvent, closeAfter), adding Reason and Event.Hook.
5. Register warden.hook.skipped.total in internal/observability.
6. Write internal/proxy/hooks_post_test.go and extend BenchmarkHandleHTTPKeepAlive coverage.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] A buffered JSON response denied by a post hook returns 502, the original body is never written, the event has Reason hook_denied, and the next keep-alive request dials a fresh upstream: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestPostHook_BufferedDeny`.
- [ ] An SSE MCP response with an allowing post hook is relayed unchanged; with a denying hook nothing is relayed and a JSON-RPC error is returned: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestPostHook_Streamed`.
- [ ] The Input captured by a remote post hook has status and data classes but no response body bytes: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestPostHook_NoBodyToRemote`.
- [ ] A post hook exceeding the 300ms post budget follows its failMode with kind budget: `go test ./internal/hooks -run TestChain_PostBudget`.
- [ ] With no post hooks, `go test ./internal/proxy -run '^$' -bench BenchmarkHandleHTTPKeepAlive -benchmem` shows no extra allocs/op compared with main.

**Depends on:** [`W-P4-HOOK-07`](policy-hooks.md#711--w-p4-hook-07) Wire the pre-request hook stage into the HTTP/1.1 proxy path

**Unblocks:** [`W-P4-HOOK-06`](policy-hooks.md#611--w-p4-hook-06) Write operator docs and the hook input schema

### 7/11 · W-P4-HOOK-07

**Wire the pre-request hook stage into the HTTP/1.1 proxy path**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#332](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/332)

Add the `hookGate` stage to runRequestStages after dlpScan and before swapSecrets, hold the Chain on Proxy, and rebuild it from settings and local YAML. Paths not yet wired (h2, WebSocket, raw tunnels, non-TLS) fail closed with hook_uninspectable when a pre hook matches, through a new `hooks` value in the deferred enum, so no protocol can skip a hook. The worker reports the `hooks/v1` capability.

**Requirements**

- New atomic holder `hooksP` with `Proxy.SetHooks(*hooks.Chain)`, snapshotted once per request on requestScope. With no chain the stage is one atomic load and a nil check with 0 extra allocations.
- hookGate builds Input from s.domain, s.port, the method, the pre-swap auditURL path (W-P1-JAUD-05), the MCP tool (or protocol.IsMCP when s.gw is nil), DLP classes, finding kinds and identity.Subject from connIdentity. It is never reached when policy, block list, identity, judge, MCP or DLP deny.
- Deny writes 403 JSON `{"error":"hook_denied","hook":"<name>"}` (reason only with exposeReason) through writeErrorResponse and stores one event via recordEvent with Reason hook_denied or hook_unavailable; RecordBlocked uses the same constant. FailOpen hooks are recorded in Event.HookFailOpen on allowed events.
- Add hook_denied, hook_unavailable and hook_uninspectable to internal/proxy/reasons.go; add Event.Hook, Event.HookReason and Event.HookFailOpen (json omitempty, additive SQLite and fleet columns); map them into auditlog.Record and docs/schemas/warden.decision.v1.json (fields hook, hook_reason, hook_fail_open) with a schema_rev bump.
- Extend the W-P1-GPOL-03 `deferred` enum with `hooks`: when a pre hook matches the CONNECT destination, a raw tunnel (no CA), non-TLS or unknown-protocol branch, an h2 connection and a WebSocket upgrade are denied with hook_uninspectable instead of passed.
- SettingsApplier.Apply and the standalone boot wiring build the chain only when the canonical hash of the hooks block changes. A hook that fails to build keeps its previous compiled version with one WARN; with no previous version an always-error placeholder is installed so failMode decides.
- RemoteProvider.Heartbeat adds `hooks/v1` to the caps list from W-P1-BLOCK-02.
- With no hooks configured, existing proxy tests stay green and the stage list behaves byte-identically.

**Implementation plan**

1. Add the hooksP holder, SetHooks and a hooks() accessor in internal/proxy/proxy.go next to SetJudge and SetSecrets.
2. Add new internal/proxy/hooks.go with hookGate and buildHookInput; insert hookGate into runRequestStages in internal/proxy/http.go between dlpScan and swapSecrets.
3. Add the three reasons to internal/proxy/reasons.go, the Event fields in internal/analytics/analytics.go and the SQLite columns, and the auditlog mapping and schema enum entries.
4. Add `hooks` to the deferred enum in handleConn/handleTLS (internal/proxy/serve.go, tls.go) and fail closed in serveGRPCStream, handleWSUpgrade and the tunnel path with hook_uninspectable.
5. In internal/worker/applier.go Apply, hash the hooks block, call hooks.Build with the previous chain for fallback, and SetHooks; mirror it in internal/worker/wiring.go for local YAML.
6. Add `hooks/v1` to the heartbeat caps in internal/config/remote.go RemoteProvider.Heartbeat.
7. Write internal/proxy/hooks_test.go and internal/worker/applier_hooks_test.go.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] A policy-allowed request with a denying fake pre hook gets 403, swapSecrets and the upstream dial never run, and one event has Reason hook_denied and Hook set: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestHookGate_DenyBlocksBeforeSwap`.
- [ ] Requests denied by policy at CONNECT, the block list, the judge, the MCP gateway or DLP enforce reach the fake hook 0 times: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestHookGate_NeverReachedOnUpstreamDeny`.
- [ ] A request with a secret placeholder in its query gives an Input with the pre-swap path, no query, no header, body or token: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestHookGate_InputIsBoundedMetadata`.
- [ ] With a pre hook matching the domain, a raw tunnel without a CA, an h2 connection and a WebSocket upgrade are each denied with hook_uninspectable: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestHookGate_UninspectableFailsClosed`.
- [ ] A settings apply with a broken hook keeps the previous hook, and a first apply with a broken failMode-closed hook denies with hook_unavailable: `go test ./internal/worker -run TestApplier_HookBuildFailure`.

### 8/11 · W-P4-HOOK-08

**Run hooks at CONNECT, per h2 stream and on MCP over WebSocket and stdio**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#333](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/333)

Close the coverage gaps that W-P4-HOOK-07 fails closed: run `connect` hooks in handleConn before any dial, run pre hooks per h2 stream in serveGRPCStream, and run tool-matching pre hooks for MCP over WebSocket and the local stdio wrapper through a gateway decorator. Raw tunnels and non-TLS traffic still fail closed when a request-level pre hook matches, because they cannot be inspected; connect hooks cover them instead.

**Requirements**

- `stage: connect` hooks run in handleConn after the block-list, identity and policy checks and before any dial or `200 Connection Established`, with Input limited to domain, port, protocol and identity, under hooksBudget.connect. A deny writes 403 and stores an event with Reason hook_denied, on every path including raw tunnels.
- serveGRPCStream runs the pre chain per stream after identity and before the metadata swap and copyGRPCHeaders, with method POST and the :path without query. A deny answers that stream 403 and stores the same event shape as HTTP/1.1; h2 no longer fails closed with hook_uninspectable.
- A new decorator in internal/proxy wraps MCPGateway.OnRequest: when the gateway verdict passes and a pre hook matches the tool, it runs the chain and returns a deny verdict with Reason hook_denied. It promotes ScansWSFrames so the WS pump keeps frame scanning, and WS upgrades no longer fail closed for tool-matching hooks.
- cmd/proxy/mcp.go builds a chain from the local `hooks:` block (in-process types and webhook) and wraps the stdio gateway with the same decorator; without hooks the stdio path is unchanged.
- Hook denies on these paths increment the same metrics with stage connect or pre and record added_latency stage=hooks_connect or hooks_pre.
- With no hooks configured, the CONNECT, gRPC and WS paths are unchanged with 0 extra allocations.

**Implementation plan**

1. Add a connectHookGate call in handleConn (internal/proxy/serve.go) after the policy decision and before tunnel/handleTLS.
2. Add the per-stream hook call at the top of serveGRPCStream in internal/proxy/grpc.go and remove h2 from the hook_uninspectable branch.
3. Add new hookGateway decorator in internal/proxy/hooks_mcp.go implementing MCPGateway and WSScanner; apply it in SetMCPGateway when a chain with tool-matching hooks is present, and re-apply on SetHooks.
4. Wrap the gateway in cmd/proxy/mcp.go runMCP before building stdio.Pump.
5. Write internal/proxy/hooks_connect_test.go, grpc hook tests and WS/stdio decorator tests.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] A connect hook denying a domain blocks a raw tunnel before any dial, with Reason hook_denied: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestConnectHook_DeniesTunnel`.
- [ ] An h2 stream to an allowed domain with a denying pre hook gets 403, no upstream stream opens, and the Input shows the placeholder name, not the secret value: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestGRPCHookGate`.
- [ ] An MCP tools/call over WebSocket and over the stdio pump is denied by a tool-matching hook, and frame scanning still runs: `go test ./internal/proxy ./cmd/proxy -run TestMCPHookDecorator`.
- [ ] With no hooks, `go test ./internal/proxy -run '^$' -bench 'BenchmarkHandleHTTP|BenchmarkGRPC' -benchmem` shows no extra allocs/op compared with main.

### 10/11 · W-P4-HOOK-10

**Guard hook settings on the CP with validation, roles, audit and capability checks**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#335](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/335)

A hook URL receives identity metadata and a failMode-closed hook can deny the whole fleet, so the CP must control who edits hooks and refuse configs that part of the fleet would silently ignore. The CP validates hooks with the shared validator at save, makes the field admin-only and audited, and refuses hook changes while a connected worker lacks `hooks/v1`.

**Requirements**

- The settings save path (POST/PUT /dashboard/api/settings and a held draft applied under p2-approvals) runs config.ValidateHooks; invalid hooks return 400 with the hook name and error.

- Every hooks change writes a p1-admin-audit record listing hook names, types, stages and URL hosts only, never full URLs, expressions or module source.
- A save that adds or changes hooks returns 409 `{"error":"workers_lack_capability","workers":[ids]}` when a connected worker lacks `hooks/v1`; `force=true` overrides for admins only and the audit record notes force and the worker ids (the W-P2-WBND-07 pattern).
- The fleet view shows a `no hooks` badge for workers without the cap while the served settings contain hooks.
- Tests lock in that the approvals classifier treats any hooks change as widening `settings.changed`, and policyeval replay output states that hooks were not replayed.

**Implementation plan**

1. Call config.ValidateHooks in the CP settings write handler in internal/controlplane.
2. Add hooks and hooksBudget to the admin-only field list from W-P1-SSO-05.
3. Add the audit record through the W-P1-AAUD-02 middleware with a host-only summary helper.
4. Add the capability check next to the W-P2-WBND-07 require-mode check, reading caps from the worker registry.
5. Add the fleet badge and a policyeval note `hooks_not_replayed` in internal/policyeval output.
6. Write internal/controlplane tests for 400, 403, 409, force and the audit record.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] An editor saving hooks gets 403 and an admin gets 200 with one audit record that contains the URL host but not the path or query: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestSettingsHooks_AdminOnlyAudited`.
- [ ] With a connected worker lacking hooks/v1, a hooks save returns 409 workers_lack_capability, and an admin force succeeds and is audited: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestSettingsHooks_CapabilityGuard`.
- [ ] A CEL syntax error is rejected at save with 400 naming the hook: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestSettingsHooks_Validation`.
- [ ] The approvals classifier marks a hooks change as widening: `go test ./internal/controlplane/... -run TestClassify_HooksWidening`.

### 11/11 · W-P4-HOOK-11

**Add embedded OPA hook mode with restricted builtins**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#336](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/336)

Add `mode: embedded` to the OPA hook type so rego runs in-process without a separate service. Modules travel inline in settings so they are signed and go through approvals, and the query is prepared with capabilities that remove environment and network builtins, so a policy cannot read worker secrets or send tool args out. Split from W-P4-HOOK-04 because it adds a large dependency and its own sandboxing.

**Requirements**

- Uses github.com/open-policy-agent/opa/v1/rego (v1 rego syntax), pinned to a release at least two weeks old. The PR records the binary size change; if it is over 10 MiB, embedded mode goes behind a build tag documented in the PR and docs.
- Config `modules: {name: source}` inline in settings, capped at 256 KiB total. `bundlePath` (directory or tar.gz, max 8 MiB) is accepted only from standalone local YAML and rejected in SettingsWire.
- Queries are prepared once per apply with rego.Capabilities that remove opa.runtime, http.send, net.*, print and trace, and with rego.StrictBuiltinErrors(true). A module using a removed builtin fails validation on the CP and the worker.
- Evaluation uses PreparedEvalQuery.Eval with the hook deadline and the shared result parser from W-P4-HOOK-04; includeArgs is allowed.
- Reload: a changed module set re-prepares and swaps; a failed prepare keeps the previous query with kind build and one WARN, and with no previous query the always-error placeholder applies. Standalone bundlePath reloads on policy reload only.
- Performance: embedded evaluation of the sample policy is p99 under 1ms.

**Implementation plan**

1. Add github.com/open-policy-agent/opa to go.mod and measure the worker binary size before and after.
2. Add new internal/hooks/opa_embedded.go: build restricted capabilities from ast.CapabilitiesForThisVersion, prepare rego.New(rego.Query("data."+path), rego.Module(...)...).PrepareForEval(ctx).
3. Enable `embedded` in the opa mode switch from W-P4-HOOK-04 and extend config.ValidateHooks with the modules cap and the bundlePath local-only rule.
4. Write internal/hooks/opa_embedded_test.go with a parity table against the REST parser, sandbox tests and BenchmarkOPAEmbedded.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] The same policy served by an httptest /v1/data server and loaded inline gives the same decision and reason for a table of 10 inputs: `go test ./internal/hooks -run TestOPA_RestEmbeddedParity`.
- [ ] A module calling opa.runtime(), http.send or net.lookup_ip_addr fails validation: `go test ./internal/hooks -run TestOPAEmbedded_RestrictedBuiltins`.
- [ ] A settings apply with a new module set uses the new policy on the next request, and a broken module keeps the old one with kind build: `go test ./internal/hooks -run TestOPAEmbedded_Reload`.
- [ ] bundlePath in SettingsWire fails validation: `go test ./internal/config -run TestHooksConfig_OPAEmbedded`.
